name: Euclid's infinitude of primes
what_was_creative: Instead of listing primes, assumes a finite list and constructs a number (product+1) none of them divides
reusable_lesson: Turn 'infinitely many X' into 'any finite list of X can be extended' and build the witness explicitly
ai_relevance: Template for constructive extension arguments; easy Lean target (Nat.exists_infinite_primes)

name: Archimedes' Method of mechanical theorems
what_was_creative: Found areas/volumes (e.g. sphere = 2/3 cylinder) by imagined balancing of infinitesimal slices on a lever, then proved them rigorously by exhaustion; text survived only in a palimpsest rediscovered by Heiberg 1906
reusable_lesson: Separate discovery from proof: use a heuristic physical model to guess the answer, then prove it with a rigorous method
ai_relevance: Agents should run cheap heuristic 'discovery' models (numerics, physics analogies) before attempting formal proof
reference: The Method (Archimedes Palimpsest); Heiberg 1906; Netz & Noel, The Archimedes Codex (2007)

name: Brachistochrone via optics
what_was_creative: Modeled the falling bead as a light ray in a medium of varying density and applied Fermat's least-time principle / Snell's law to get the cycloid
reusable_lesson: A variational problem in one field may already be solved by a principle in another; map the objective to a known extremal principle
ai_relevance: Prompt agents to ask 'what physical system optimizes this same functional?'

name: Seven Bridges of Königsberg
what_was_creative: Discarded geometry entirely and kept only adjacency; reduced the walk question to vertex-degree parity
reusable_lesson: Strip a problem to the minimal structure that matters; the answer often becomes a parity count
ai_relevance: Abstraction step: ask agents to produce the most stripped-down model before searching
reference: Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (1736)

name: Constructibility of the 17-gon
what_was_creative: Translated a ruler-and-compass question into the algebra of roots of unity and successive quadratic extensions (Gauss periods)
reusable_lesson: Change the language: geometric constructibility = field-extension degree questions
ai_relevance: Agents should look for an algebraic encoding of geometric/combinatorial constraints

name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
what_was_creative: Used analysis (L-functions, characters) to prove a purely arithmetic statement
reusable_lesson: Import analytic tools (generating functions, Fourier/characters) into discrete problems
ai_relevance: Agents should try generating-function / Fourier encodings for counting problems
reference: Dirichlet, Abh. Königl. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. (1837)

name: Galois theory and unsolvability of the quintic
what_was_creative: Replaced the search for formulas with the study of the symmetry group of the roots; solvability by radicals = solvable group
reusable_lesson: Attach a symmetry object to the problem and translate the question into a property of that object
ai_relevance: Ask agents: what group/automorphism structure does this object carry?

name: Cantor's diagonal argument
what_was_creative: Builds an element differing from the n-th listed item at position n, so no list is complete
reusable_lesson: To show no enumeration/function covers everything, diagonalize against an arbitrary candidate
ai_relevance: Reusable template for impossibility/lower-bound proofs; well-supported in Lean (Function.cantor_surjective)

name: Fifteen puzzle unsolvability
people: W. W. Johnson; W. E. Story
what_was_creative: Permutation parity plus blank-position parity is an invariant of legal moves, so half of configurations are unreachable
reusable_lesson: Find the right invariant: a quantity preserved by every move that distinguishes start from target
ai_relevance: Invariant search is mechanizable: agents can propose candidate invariants and check them on move sets

name: Dehn invariant and Hilbert's third problem
what_was_creative: Introduced an invariant of polyhedra preserved under scissors-congruence; cube and regular tetrahedron differ, so equal volumes need not be equidecomposable
reusable_lesson: Design a new invariant tailored to the allowed operations
ai_relevance: Same as above: invariant design as an explicit agent subtask

name: Sperner's lemma proof of Brouwer fixed point
what_was_creative: A combinatorial parity-counting lemma on labeled triangulations yields Brouwer's topological fixed point theorem
reusable_lesson: Discretize a continuous problem and use a counting/parity argument, then pass to a limit
ai_relevance: Discretization makes topological statements amenable to finite search and formal proof

name: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
what_was_creative: Arithmetized syntax (Gödel numbering) so a formula can talk about its own provability
reusable_lesson: Encode the meta-level inside the object level, then apply diagonalization
ai_relevance: Foundation for understanding limits of automated provers; formalized in several proof assistants

name: Mutilated chessboard
people: Max Black (puzzle); popularized by Gamow & Stern, Golomb
what_was_creative: Coloring argument: each domino covers one black and one white square, but two same-colored corners were removed
reusable_lesson: A coloring/weighting turns an exhaustive search into a one-line counting invariant
ai_relevance: Known benchmark where naive automated search is hard but the human invariant is trivial; a test for agent 'insight'
reference: Black, Critical Thinking (1946); McCarthy 1964 on ATP difficulty

name: Erdős probabilistic lower bound for Ramsey numbers
what_was_creative: Showed a random 2-coloring of K_n has no monochromatic K_k with positive probability, proving R(k,k) > 2^(k/2) without constructing a coloring
reusable_lesson: Existence by showing a random object works with positive probability
ai_relevance: Agents should try 'pick randomly and compute expectation' when explicit constructions fail

name: Furstenberg's topological proof of infinitely many primes
what_was_creative: Defined a topology on the integers via arithmetic progressions; finitely many primes would make a non-open set open
reusable_lesson: Re-cast a statement in an unexpected structure (topology) where it becomes a short contradiction
ai_relevance: Exploration heuristic: try embedding the problem into a different category and look for contradictions

name: Four Color Theorem (Appel–Haken)
what_was_creative: Reduced the problem to checking ~1,900 reducible configurations by computer, using discharging to prove unavoidability
reusable_lesson: Reduce infinitely many cases to a finite unavoidable set, then let the computer check each
ai_relevance: Model for human-designed reduction + machine-checked cases

name: Four Color Theorem in Coq
what_was_creative: Fully formalized the (Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas) proof in Coq, including the computational part, using small-scale reflection
reusable_lesson: Make brute force trustworthy by running it inside a proof assistant (proof by reflection)
ai_relevance: Direct template: verified decision procedures in Lean (decide / native_decide / certified checkers)

name: Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemerédi's theorem
what_was_creative: Correspondence principle turns density questions on integers into multiple recurrence in measure-preserving systems
reusable_lesson: Transfer a combinatorial problem to dynamics where powerful structure theorems exist
ai_relevance: Agents should maintain a 'dictionary' of known correspondences between fields

name: Marjorie Rice's pentagon tilings
what_was_creative: A homemaker with no formal training found four new types of convex pentagons that tile the plane using her own notation
reusable_lesson: Fresh notation and persistence from outsiders can open closed-looking classifications
ai_relevance: Value of unconventional representations; agents can explore with their own encodings

name: Mirror symmetry count of rational curves on the quintic
people: Philip Candelas; Xenia de la Ossa; Paul Green; Linda Parkes
what_was_creative: String theory duality predicted the numbers of rational curves of every degree on the quintic threefold, far beyond what geometers could compute; later proven (Givental; Lian–Liu–Yau)
reusable_lesson: A duality can convert a hard count into an easy computation on the dual side
ai_relevance: Agents should look for dual formulations where the computation is tractable
reference: Candelas et al., Nucl. Phys. B 359 (1991)

name: Monstrous moonshine (Borcherds)
what_was_creative: Proved the Conway–Norton conjecture using vertex operator algebras and the no-ghost theorem from string theory
reusable_lesson: Numerical coincidences (196884 = 196883+1) signal a hidden structure worth building
ai_relevance: Numerical pattern matching across tables of constants is an agent-friendly discovery task

name: Fermat's Last Theorem via modularity
what_was_creative: Linked Fermat solutions to elliptic curves (Frey, Ribet) and proved semistable modularity, so a counterexample would yield an impossible non-modular curve
reusable_lesson: Translate the problem into a different conjecture inside a richer theory, then prove that
ai_relevance: Shows value of long reduction chains; Lean formalization project led by Kevin Buzzard is ongoing

name: Robbins conjecture by automated prover EQP
what_was_creative: An automated equational theorem prover found a proof that Robbins algebras are Boolean, open since the 1930s
reusable_lesson: Some purely equational problems are within reach of uniform search with good heuristics
ai_relevance: Equational reasoning is a strong niche for machine search; precursor to the Equational Theories Project

name: Kepler conjecture (Hales)
what_was_creative: Reduced sphere packing optimality to a finite but huge set of nonlinear inequalities checked by linear programming and interval arithmetic
reusable_lesson: Turn an infinite optimization into finitely many certified numerical checks
ai_relevance: Interval arithmetic + LP certificates are reusable machine-checkable proof components

name: Flyspeck: formal proof of Kepler
what_was_creative: After referees could not fully verify the computer proof, the team formalized it in HOL Light and Isabelle
reusable_lesson: When human review is the bottleneck, formal verification is the way to close the proof
ai_relevance: Exact motivation for our Lean pipeline: formalize computer-assisted proofs
reference: Hales et al., Forum of Math, Pi 5 (2017)

name: Perelman's proof of the Poincaré conjecture
what_was_creative: Used Ricci flow (a heat-like PDE on metrics) with surgery; introduced an entropy-like monotone functional inspired by statistical mechanics
reusable_lesson: Evolve the object with a flow that smooths it, and find a monotone quantity controlling the flow
ai_relevance: Look for monotone functionals/potential functions along a process

name: Dvir's finite field Kakeya
what_was_creative: A low-degree polynomial vanishing on a Kakeya set must vanish everywhere, giving a near-sharp bound in a short proof
reusable_lesson: Find a low-degree polynomial vanishing on the set and use degree counting to get a contradiction
ai_relevance: Polynomial-method templates are short and very suitable for formalization

name: Zhang's bounded gaps between primes
what_was_creative: A little-known lecturer outside the research mainstream proved infinitely many prime gaps below 70 million by refining GPY sieve with a smooth-moduli equidistribution estimate
reusable_lesson: Small technical improvements on a near-miss method can break a barrier
ai_relevance: Agents should scan 'almost-works' methods for the missing estimate

name: Maynard–Tao multidimensional sieve
what_was_creative: Changed the sieve weights to multidimensional ones, getting gaps ≤ 600 with a simpler argument that avoided Zhang's hardest step
reusable_lesson: A better choice of auxiliary object (weights) can make the hard part unnecessary
ai_relevance: Optimization over auxiliary functions is a numerical task agents can do

name: Polymath8: bounded gaps reduced to 246
what_was_creative: Open online collaboration rapidly optimized Zhang's and Maynard's bounds down to 246
reusable_lesson: Many small parallel improvements on a modular argument compound quickly
ai_relevance: Model for multi-agent work: shared blueprint, modular sub-bounds, public log

name: Polymath1: density Hales–Jewett
what_was_creative: First Polymath: open blog collaboration found a new elementary combinatorial proof of DHJ(3) in weeks
reusable_lesson: Publicly decompose a problem into small comments; fast feedback beats lone deep work
ai_relevance: Template for agent swarms with shared notes and frequent small contributions

name: Erdős discrepancy problem
people: Terence Tao (after Polymath5; SAT case by Konev & Lisitsa 2014)
what_was_creative: SAT showed discrepancy 2 sequences have length ≤1160; Tao's full proof used an entropy decrement argument and a reduction to a form of the Elliott conjecture suggested by a blog comment
reusable_lesson: Use computation to probe small cases, then a bridge to analytic number theory for the general case
ai_relevance: Combine SAT experiments with human/AI conceptual reduction
reference: Tao, Discrete Analysis 2016:1; Konev & Lisitsa, SAT 2014

name: Boolean Pythagorean triples
people: Marijn Heule; Oliver Kullmann; Victor Marek
what_was_creative: Showed 1..7824 can be 2-colored with no monochromatic Pythagorean triple but 1..7825 cannot, via cube-and-conquer SAT; certificate ~200 TB
reusable_lesson: Encode as SAT, split with cube-and-conquer, and emit a checkable DRAT proof
ai_relevance: Direct playbook: SAT encoding + verified proof checker (e.g. cake_lpr) + Lean bridge

name: Schur number five
what_was_creative: Proved S(5)=160 by SAT with symmetry breaking; proof certificate ~2 petabytes, verified by a formally verified checker
reusable_lesson: Symmetry breaking and verified checkers make enormous searches credible
ai_relevance: Agents should exploit symmetry before brute force

name: Cap set problem via polynomial method
people: Ernie Croot; Vsevolod Lev; Péter Pál Pach; Jordan Ellenberg; Dion Gijswijt
what_was_creative: Croot–Lev–Pach's slice-rank-type polynomial argument for Z_4^n was adapted within weeks by Ellenberg–Gijswijt to F_3^n, giving an exponential improvement in a 3-page proof
reusable_lesson: When a new technique appears, immediately test it on neighboring problems
ai_relevance: Agents should port a new trick to every related open problem
reference: Ellenberg & Gijswijt, Annals 185 (2017); Croot, Lev & Pach, Annals 185 (2017)

name: Viazovska's sphere packing in dimension 8 (and 24)
people: Maryna Viazovska; with Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko for dim 24
what_was_creative: Constructed the 'magic function' required by the Cohn–Elkies LP bound using modular forms
reusable_lesson: Reduce optimality to existence of an auxiliary function, then build it from a rich special-function theory
ai_relevance: Searching for certificate functions (with numerics guiding) is a promising AI task
reference: Viazovska, Annals 185 (2017); Cohn et al., Annals 185 (2017)

name: Chromatic number of the plane ≥ 5
what_was_creative: A biologist built a 1581-vertex unit-distance graph needing 5 colors, verified by SAT; Polymath16 then shrank the graph
reusable_lesson: Outsider builds a big explicit witness; computers verify; community optimizes
ai_relevance: Agents can generate large witnesses and hand them to SAT for checking

name: Sensitivity conjecture
what_was_creative: Two-page proof via a signed adjacency matrix of the hypercube and Cauchy interlacing, after ~30 years
reusable_lesson: Look for a clever linear-algebra encoding (signed matrices, spectra) of a combinatorial quantity
ai_relevance: Short proofs exist for hard problems; agents should try spectral encodings

name: Keller's conjecture in dimension 7
people: Joshua Brakensiek; Marijn Heule; John Mackey; David Narváez
what_was_creative: Resolved the last open dimension (true in dim 7) by reducing to clique existence in Keller graphs and solving with SAT plus symmetry breaking
reusable_lesson: Combine structural reductions with SAT and a verified certificate
ai_relevance: Another SAT + verified-checker template

name: Kaplansky unit conjecture counterexample
what_was_creative: Encoded existence of a nontrivial unit in a group ring of the Hantzsche–Wendt group as SAT; solver found it
reusable_lesson: Semi-decidable 'find a counterexample' problems in algebra can be SAT-encoded
ai_relevance: Agents should encode bounded-support counterexample searches as SAT

name: Machine learning guiding knot theory and representation theory
people: Alex Davies et al. (DeepMind); Marc Lackenby; Geordie Williamson; András Juhász
what_was_creative: Supervised learning plus attribution found that the knot signature relates to geometric invariants (natural slope), leading to a proven theorem; also guided progress on combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
reusable_lesson: Train a model to predict invariant A from B, use saliency to find which features matter, then let humans prove the relation
ai_relevance: Concrete pipeline: data generation -> prediction -> attribution -> conjecture -> proof

name: Ramanujan Machine
people: Gal Raayoni; Ido Kaminer et al.
what_was_creative: Automated search over continued fraction forms discovered new conjectured formulas for constants like e, pi, Catalan's constant
reusable_lesson: Mass numerical search for identities, followed by proof attempts of survivors
ai_relevance: Cheap high-precision numerics as conjecture generator for agents

name: Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks
what_was_creative: Used reinforcement learning (cross-entropy method) to find counterexamples to several published graph-theory conjectures
reusable_lesson: Turn 'disprove conjecture' into maximizing a score that is positive iff counterexample
ai_relevance: Directly reusable: write a score function, run RL/evolutionary search

name: Heesch number 6
what_was_creative: Found a polyform with Heesch number 6, the highest known, extending computer searches started by Casey Mann
reusable_lesson: Systematic computer search over shape families finds record witnesses
ai_relevance: Record-hunting tasks are well suited to search agents

name: Liquid Tensor Experiment
people: Peter Scholze (challenge); Johan Commelin et al. (Lean community)
what_was_creative: Scholze asked for a formal check of a key theorem he was unsure about; Lean community verified it (main part 2021, completed 2022), clarifying the proof along the way
reusable_lesson: Formalization as a tool for the author's own confidence and for simplifying a proof
ai_relevance: Shows Lean + blueprint can handle cutting-edge abstract math
reference: Scholze, Xena blog Dec 2020; Commelin et al., github.com/leanprover-community/lean-liquid

name: AlphaTensor matrix multiplication
what_was_creative: Framed finding matrix multiplication algorithms as a single-player game of tensor decomposition; found 47-multiplication 4x4 algorithm over GF(2)
reusable_lesson: Reformulate algorithm discovery as a game with a verifiable score and use RL
ai_relevance: The output is a certificate (a decomposition) that is trivially checkable

name: PFR conjecture and its Lean formalization
people: Timothy Gowers; Ben Green; Freddie Manners; Terence Tao
what_was_creative: Proved Marton's polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over F_2 using entropy methods; a crowd formalization in Lean with a blueprint finished in about three weeks
reusable_lesson: Blueprint (dependency graph of lemmas) lets many contributors formalize in parallel
ai_relevance: Direct model for our agents: blueprint + Lean + parallel lemma assignment
reference: Gowers et al., arXiv:2311.05762; Tao blog Dec 2023

name: The einstein 'hat' aperiodic monotile
people: David Smith; Joseph Samuel Myers; Craig S. Kaplan; Chaim Goodman-Strauss
what_was_creative: A hobbyist found the shape by experimenting with software; proofs used computer-assisted combinatorics and a geometric incommensurability argument; followed by the chiral 'spectre'
reusable_lesson: Exploration by play with good tools finds candidates; experts then prove
ai_relevance: Agents can run open-ended exploration with visual/software tools and flag anomalies
reference: Smith et al., Combinatorial Theory 4 (2024), arXiv:2303.10798

name: FunSearch cap sets
people: Bernardino Romera-Paredes et al. (DeepMind); Jordan Ellenberg
what_was_creative: LLM evolved programs (not objects) that generate cap sets, finding a size-512 cap set in dimension 8, larger than previously known
reusable_lesson: Search over programs that construct objects; programs are interpretable and generalize
ai_relevance: Core playbook: LLM proposes code, evaluator scores, evolutionary loop

name: AlphaGeometry
people: Trieu Trinh; Yuhuai Wu; Quoc Le; He He; Thang Luong
what_was_creative: Neuro-symbolic: symbolic deduction engine plus a language model trained on synthetic data that proposes auxiliary constructions; solved 25 of 30 IMO geometry problems
reusable_lesson: Let the model propose creative auxiliary objects, let a symbolic engine do the deductions
ai_relevance: Split creativity (LLM) from verification (symbolic engine)

name: Empty hexagon theorem
what_was_creative: Proved every set of 30 points in general position contains an empty convex hexagon via SAT, with the encoding itself verified in Lean
reusable_lesson: Verify both the SAT certificate and the encoding (the weakest link) formally
ai_relevance: Exact template for SAT + Lean integration
reference: Heule & Scheucher, TACAS 2024; Subercaseaux et al., ITP 2024 (Lean verification)

name: AlphaProof at IMO 2024
what_was_creative: RL agent trained on millions of auto-formalized problems produced Lean proofs for 4 of 6 IMO 2024 problems (silver-medal level)
reusable_lesson: Train by self-play in a formal system: the proof checker is the reward signal
ai_relevance: Lean as a reward function is our core architecture
reference: DeepMind blog July 2024; Hubert et al., Nature (2025)

name: Busy Beaver BB(5)
what_was_creative: Online collaboration (many amateurs) classified all 5-state 2-symbol Turing machines and proved BB(5) = 47,176,870 with a Coq proof
reusable_lesson: Crowdsourced deciders + formal verification can settle massive case analyses
ai_relevance: Combining many heuristic deciders, each proved correct, is a scalable agent pattern

name: Equational Theories Project
what_was_creative: Settled all ~22 million implications between 4694 magma laws using humans, ATPs, SAT/countermodel finders and Lean verification
reusable_lesson: Massive uniform micro-problems are ideal for a mixed human+automation pipeline with Lean as the final arbiter
ai_relevance: Closest existing analogue of an ESH27 swarm

name: Kakeya conjecture in R^3
what_was_creative: Proved Kakeya sets in R^3 have Hausdorff dimension 3 via multiscale induction on 'sticky' vs non-sticky configurations
reusable_lesson: Split into structured vs unstructured cases and induct across scales
ai_relevance: Case decomposition by structure is a strategy agents can propose explicitly

name: AlphaEvolve: 4x4 complex matrix multiplication and kissing number
what_was_creative: LLM-driven evolutionary coding agent found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices and a 593-sphere configuration improving the kissing number lower bound in 11 dimensions
reusable_lesson: Evolve code with an automatic evaluator; works for any problem with a scoreable construction
ai_relevance: Directly reusable loop for bound-improvement tasks
reference: DeepMind, AlphaEvolve white paper May 2025; arXiv:2506.13131

name: Erdős problems and LLM-assisted literature search
people: Users of erdosproblems.com; Thomas Bloom; Terence Tao
what_was_creative: Oct 2025 claims that GPT-5 'solved' Erdős problems turned out to be LLM literature search finding existing solutions to problems listed as open
reusable_lesson: Before attacking a problem, have an AI search the literature: many 'open' problems are already solved
ai_relevance: Mandatory first step for agents: literature search, then claim nothing without checking

name: Erdős problem #728 solved by AI
people: Kevin Barreto; GPT-5.2 Pro; Harmonic's Aristotle
what_was_creative: Informal argument by an LLM was formalized in Lean by Aristotle; considered among the first autonomous AI solutions of an Erdős problem (after interpretation of the statement was clarified)
reusable_lesson: LLM proposes informal proof, formal agent verifies; statement interpretation must be fixed precisely
ai_relevance: Exactly our pipeline: informal reasoning -> Lean -> human audit of statement

name: Noperthedron: polyhedron without Rupert's property
what_was_creative: Constructed a convex polyhedron (90 vertices) and proved it cannot pass through itself, combining theory with a large computer search over orientations
reusable_lesson: Theory reduces a continuous parameter space to a finite grid; computation covers the grid
ai_relevance: Pattern: Lipschitz/error bounds turn continuous search into a finite certified search

name: Proofs without words
what_was_creative: Identities such as sum of odd numbers = n^2 shown by a single picture or bijection
reusable_lesson: A bijection or picture often explains why an identity holds; turn it into a combinatorial proof
ai_relevance: Agents can search for bijective proofs, which often formalize cleanly
